newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm also relative to German Bunds, which ended a touch weaker.
U.S. bonds remained slightly firm despite news U.S. first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) was revised up to show a gain of 5.9 percent from a preliminary rise of 5.8 percent.

One Swiss-based trader said, looking at latest GDP data that he would not rule out an increase in U.S. interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets next Tuesday and Wednesday. But most economists expect no tightening at the July meeting, given a slight slowdown seen in other U.S. data of late.
Swiss traders said volumes were extremely thin, partly due to lack of investor interest tied to low yields.

EuroSwiss futures on LIFFE were a shade softer in late trade. One trader said the Sept contract now appeared in an upward channel, with a strong close above 98.60 potentially signaling an upmove towards 98.90. A break below 98.47/48 could launch a move back to 98.00, he said.
Comi medium-term bond up four at 113.54
Euro Swiss francs off one at 98.56.
